title: How to jump-start a car safely
metaDesc: How to jump-start a car safely: check the battery first, connect the cables in the right order, start it, and take the cables off in reverse.
first: Only jump-start where you have room to work away from traffic. If you don't, call roadside help.
Look at the dead battery first. If it's cracked, bulging or smells like rotten eggs, don't jump it. Call for help.
Check your owner's manual. Some cars have special jump points under the hood, and many hybrids and electric cars shouldn't be used to jump another car.
Both cars: in Park (or neutral), parking brake on, engines and everything else off.
Wear safety glasses if you have them, and take off rings and watches.
dont: Don't jump a battery that's cracked, bulging or smells like rotten eggs.
Don't clip the last black clamp to the dead battery. Use bare metal on the dead car.
Keep the cables away from belts and fans.
Don't keep cranking a car that won't start. Three tries is enough.

steps.t: Park the good car close to the dead one, but don't let the cars touch. Both engines off, parking brakes on.
Clip one red clamp to the + post of the dead battery.
Clip the other red clamp to the + post of the good battery.
Clip one black clamp to the - post of the good battery.
Clip the last black clamp to a clean, unpainted metal bolt or bracket on the dead car's engine or frame.

Start the good car and let it run 3 to 5 minutes. Then try to start the dead car. If it cranks slowly, wait about 5 more minutes and try once more. If it still won't start after the third try, the battery probably needs replacing.

steps.h: 7. Take the cables off in reverse
steps.t: Let both cars run a few more minutes. Then take the clamps off in the exact reverse order: black from the metal, black from the good battery, red from the good battery, red from the dead battery.
Get the battery and charging system tested soon. A battery that dies again may be worn out, or the car may not be charging it.

call: Call roadside help if the battery looks damaged, you don't have cables or a helper car, you're near traffic, or it's dark or foggy.
If it still won't start after a jump, see Car won't start.
